title: Out of memory on Firefox and Chrome from version grafana:9.5.20 to latest today (11.2.2)
body:
### What happened?

I have 32 GB of memory and an Intel Core i7-10700 CPU @ 2.90GHz.  Running windows 11 latest build.  After loading a fairly complex dashboard of 30 panels, and scrolling halfway to the bottom of the dashboard, the dashboard freezes and I get a browser out of memory error message for both Chrome and Firefox.  Windows task manager reports 98% memory usage.  After closing the grafana tab, memory returns to 15% usage.  CPU usage during the grafana dashboard load remains stable.

This has been an issue for me since Grafana 9.5.2.0.  I have tried multiple new versions and always end up reverting back to 9.5.20 as this version works without error.

### What did you expect to happen?

For 11.2.2 to work without error as earlier versions do.

### Did this work before?

docker 9.5.2.0

### How do we reproduce it?

My datasources are varied for this dashboard with Prometheus and influxdb.  The Prometheus data pulls from many different exporters including SNMP, node exporter, unifi etc. InfluxDB also pulls from different databases.
2.So I suppose you could create a lengthy dashboard from different sources, and then try scrolling through every data pane.
3.


### Is the bug inside a dashboard panel?

No, this is a browser level--tab level error.

### Environment (with versions)?

Grafana: 11.2.2
OS: Windows 11 Pro 64-bit 23H2
Browser: Chrome and Firefox latest


### Grafana platform?

Docker

### Datasource(s)?

Prometheus, InfluxDB

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
@reporter, I'd suggest you use a har file sanitizer. When you search it you'll find many of them. 
i.e. https://blog.cloudflare.com/introducing-har-sanitizer-secure-har-sharing/

or you can use a script to sanitize it. 

an example script: 

```sh
#!/bin/bash

# Usage: ./obfuscate_har.sh input.har output_obfuscated.har

input_file=$1
output_file=$2
obfuscation_string="****OBFUSCATED****"

# Check if jq is installed
if ! command -v jq &> /dev/null
then
    echo "jq could not be found. Please install jq to run this script."
    exit 1
fi

# Define jq filters for obfuscating sensitive fields
jq_filter='
    .log.entries[].request.headers |= map(
        if .name == "Authorization" or .name == "Cookie" or .name == "password" or .name == "username" 
        then .value = "'$obfuscation_string'" else . end
    ) |
    .log.entries[].request.queryString |= map(
        if .name == "password" or .name == "username" 
        then .value = "'$obfuscation_string'" else . end
    ) |
    .log.entries[].response.headers |= map(
        if .name == "Set-Cookie" then .value = "'$obfuscation_string'" else . end
    ) |
    .log.entries[].response.cookies |= map(
        .value = "'$obfuscation_string'"
    )
'

# Run jq to obfuscate the .har file
jq "$jq_filter" "$input_file" > "$output_file"

echo "Obfuscated HAR file saved to: $output_file"

```

comments.author: participant4
comments.body:
@participant2 I'm mostly curious on your data. I'm wondering if just the join is not the correct transformation for you. For example, I'm wondering if `uname`, the data you are joining by, is not very unique on your prometheus data. That will balloon out the data in a join. 

Take for example this https://<redacted-host>/d/feavrpzb4wu0wa/kristina-demos?orgId=1&from=now-30d&to=now&timezone=utc&var-fruit=apple&var-fuelType=Battery%20storage&var-stand=ice-king&var-employeeLastName=Swan&editPanel=30&tab=queries

There are only two queries, that return 8 rows each. You can hide one, and click "Query Inspector > Stats" to see the row count. The Scrape Job for all of them is the same, so if you join on that, you can end up with 64 rows. Still not a big deal with 2x8 rows but surely you can see the issue with 5x200.

I'm wondering if a group by first would help if this is what's happening - grouping by last value of the uname or something like that, to be sure you're not joining by duplicates. 

Let me know what you think?

comments.body: To those running into this, you are most likely joining on a duplicated value. If this is the case, you may want to first use the Group by transformation to ensure the data you are joining on is unique. Grouping off the value you are JOINing first, and then selecting the last value of everything else, should help this quite a bit. Obviously my data set is way smaller than yours, but let me know what you find.

comments.author: participant4
comments.body:
Hello, after some internal discussion we decided we would rather keep the transformation with the updated logic, and align it with how SQL joins work. We realize this is a breaking change for some users who relied on the previous behavior, but we would ask that you use the "Group by" transformation first to ensure what you are joining by is unique before joining. Using group by to get the last value for each group, and then joining by the group, will make it equivalent to the join logic that was in place prior to the change.

Please feel free to reply if you have any other questions, and we can reopen this if we see other issues.

comments.body: @reporter Perfect, thanks! So, here are the steps I took for this. 1. Took your dashboard, imported it into a 9.5.2 version of grafana and got the result. Via the query inspector, exported out the CSV of the data with the transformations applied so we could be sure the data matched. 2. Opened the dashboard JSON in a text editor and deleted the transforms so we wouldn't get OOM'd on import 3. Imported the edited JSON into Grafana 12.2 (off `main`). Created a panel with the testdata datasource, CSV Content scenario, and added the baseline data exported in step 1 Now from here, there are a couple paths.. I think the thing that makes this confusing is the column renaming being done in the field overrides, which happens at the end of all the transformations. So, for what I have here, I just deal with the `Value #` name at the very end. I use the group by transformation to group by the name and alias, and select the last non null value for each `Value`. I then join by the name, and use an Organize Fields by Name transformation to make the names human readable. Also went through your overrides, removed the rename there and consolidated the column width and unit definitions. And I end up with the same data as what was exported from 9.5.2. Here is the debug panel export with just the transforms I described. If you would like the CSV data from what was exported from 9.5.2, let me know. [debug-Reproduced with embedded data-03_08_2025 16_34_16.json.txt.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/21568183/debug-Reproduced.with.embedded.data-03_08_2025.16_34_16.json.txt.zip) Does this help explain what to do?
